The point $P(\frac{1}{5},\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{5})$ lies on the unit circle, as shown. What is $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta ?$ Do not round your answer.

$\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222207/assets/41c6badfbcafe7bafdddca30606511d2d6c3c8bdbbcd5ec2e29ff9c4c2dd310f.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{5}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{5}.
$$

Knowing that $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we can calculate $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta :$

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{(\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{5})}=\frac{5}{2\sqrt{6}}=\frac{5\sqrt{6}}{12}
$$
